S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in the health or behavior of a family member
patient_info.stressor: Daniel’s adult daughter moved back home after a major change in her health, and he tried to steady the household while keeping his regional freight work and mentoring new drivers on track. At first he framed his increased energy as being useful, but across seven months he became persistently upbeat or irritable, slept far less than usual, took on extra route-planning and training ideas, and developed an inflated sense that he could single-handedly reorganize the company’s driver program. His distractibility began showing up in missed client details, scattered sales follow-through, and tension at home, creating real functional impairment though he remained employed and connected to family routines. He sought psychiatric care himself after noticing that his behavior no longer matched his normally calm road-tested style and that the same pattern was damaging both work and home life.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: What finally got me in here is that over these months my mind keeps jumping to every CB chirp, fuel price sign, or new idea, and I miss details I normally never miss, like a client’s delivery note or who I promised to call back.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: For months now I’ve been either too fired up, like everything is going to work out no matter what, or I’m snapping over small stuff at home and in the yard, which isn’t my usual way.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: I keep finding extra jobs for myself—rewriting route plans, checking on new drivers after hours, fixing things around the house—and I feel antsy if I sit still too long.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: I got it in my head that I could rebuild the whole driver training program myself and make it run better than the bosses ever could, even though that’s not really my lane.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: Most nights I sleep maybe three or four hours, then I’m up before daylight feeling ready to roll instead of worn out.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: At work I’ve had to have dispatch and clients repeat details I should have tracked, and a couple of my sales follow-ups slipped through because I was chasing too many ideas at once. At home, my wife and daughter have been walking on eggshells, and I can tell I’m adding strain when I’m supposed to be helping.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about seven months, since my daughter moved back home and I started trying to keep everything steady.
